record.body:
## Evidence

Candidates: C1 pointer for the wf-analyzer-ansible project (5 error outliers, one project and branch); C2 contract join key (ambiguous_share about 0.78); C3 pre-validate jira_create_issue (error_rate 0.8333, 10 of 12 calls); C4 merge or split js-extension and vm-verify-js-fixes (identical shared cost, no exclusive sessions). Skill gaps seen: $TMP undefined; no definition of pattern, noise or severity; tools[] carries no session ids so refs need report.jsonl lookups; step 5 cannot name a failing command from counts alone.

## Consequence

The skill works as a first pass but depends on the agent inventing rules, so two runs could rank differently. C2 repeats the session-id option you already declined for now; treat it as context, not a request. C1 and C3 point at repos outside this plugin.

## Follow-up

Sign off the candidate list, or ask for a fix pass on SKILL.md: define TMP via mktemp, define pattern, noise and severity, say to read report.jsonl for tool-level session refs, and define bounded slices.

payload.basis: Dry run over 243 sessions: 4 candidates each with a metric, session references and a target; 4 patterns dropped; 6 of 7 done-when criteria met (step 7 deferred to the caller). I re-checked the Bash, jira_create_issue and error-outlier numbers against a fresh run and they match.
payload.claim: The analyze-sessions skill yields 4 specific, metric-backed candidates on real data, but it lacks rules the agent had to guess: temp directory, pattern and noise, severity, and tool-level session ids.
payload.invalidated_when: SKILL.md defines the missing rules and a second dry run needs no manual report.jsonl lookups.
